sentences.text:
The brief facts of the case is that the petitioners are the accused of Giridih (T) P.S.
Case No. 221 of 2015 involving the offences punishable under Sections 420, 406, 467,
468, 471 and 120B of Indian Penal Code which include non-bailable offences.
The petitioners are resident of West Bengal and they are absconding to evade their arrest.

The I.O. submitted a requisition for issuance of warrant of arrest inter alia against the petitioners and the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Giridih being satisfied that the petitioners are absconding and evading their arrest issued non- bailable warrant of arrest vide order dated 13.08.2021.

On 21.11.2022, the I.O. prayed for issue of proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. and I.O. returned the non-bailable warrant of arrest issued against the petitioners unexecuted mentioning that the I.O. visited the house inter alia of the petitioners on 07.11.2022 for their arrest but they escaped from the place on seeing the police.
4.

The learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Giridih on seeing the different paragraphs of the case diary was satisfied about the petitioners absconding and concealing themselves from their arrest and accordingly, issued proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. for appearance of the petitioners in his court on 02.01.2023 at 11:30 A.M.
5.

It is submitted by the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the petitioners that the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate issued non- bailable warrant of arrest on the requisition made by the I.O. and without recording subjective satisfaction has issued proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. also without applying judicial mind; in a mechanical manner.

Hence, the orders dated 13.08.2021 and 21.11.2022 passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Giridih in connection with Giridih (T)
P.S. Case No. 221 of 2015 be quashed and set aside.

6. Learned Special Public Prosecutor on the other hand vehemently opposes the prayer for quashing of the orders dated 13.08.2021 and 21.11.2022 passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Giridih in connection with Giridih (T) P.S. Case No. 221 of 2015 and submits that it is undisputed fact that petitioners are accused of non-bailable offences and evading their arrest and this two ingredients are sufficient for the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate to issue warrant of arrest against the petitioners and rightly the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate has done so.
Hence, there is no illegality in the order dated 13.08.2021.

It is then submitted that, upon non-bailable warrant of arrest, having not been executed consequent upon the petitioners escaping on seeing the police and absconding and evading their arrest, the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, being satisfied about the same has issued proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. and there is no illegality in the said order either.

Hence, it is submitted that this criminal miscellaneous petition being without any merit is Samsul Alam @ Samsul Alam Khan vs The State Of Jharkhand on 19 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182224029/
2 dismissed.
7.

sentences.text: Having heard the submissions made at the Bar and after going through the materials in the record, this Court is of the considered view that since undisputedly, the petitioners are accused of several non-bailable offences and were evading arrest as was reported by the I.O. of the case and the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate from the materials placed before it became satisfied of the same and issued non-bailable warrant of arrest hence, this Court finds that there is no illegality in the order dated 13.08.2021.

Similarly, so far as the order dated 21.11.2022 is concerned, the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate on the basis of different paragraphs of the case diary as mentioned in the order concerned, was satisfied that the petitioners absconded on seeing the police from their house and evading their arrest by concealing themselves.
Therefore, being satisfied about the same, the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate issued proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. and this Court finds that there is no illegality in that order either.
8. Accordingly, this Court is of the considered view that there is no justifiable reason to interfere with either of the two orders.
9. Accordingly, this criminal miscellaneous petition being without any merit is dismissed.

(Anil Kumar Choudhary, J.) High Court of Jharkhand, Ranchi Dated the 19th August, 2023 AFR/Sonu-Gunjan/-
